parsed.summary: The file formalizes Theorem 1.1: a compact, convex, full-dimensional set S in R^n (n>0) with barycenter 0 and interior lattice points exactly {0} has volume at most (n+1)^n/n!. It also formalizes the sharpness claim: the simplex (n+1)Δ_n − (1,…,1) has barycenter 0 and volume (n+1)^n/n!, and it gives a `CenteredBody` attaining the bound. The statements look faithful; the only caveats are junk-value behaviour of `barycenter` outside the hypotheses and the misleading name `normalizedVolume`, neither of which affects the targets.

glossary.note: The name suggests a normalization, but it is plain Lebesgue volume (not multiplied by n!). `toReal` would turn ∞ into 0, but the target statements assume compactness, so the volume is finite.

Matches the standard notion when K has positive finite volume and is integrable. Otherwise it gives 0 via junk values (⁻¹ of 0, non-integrable integral = 0). Every target statement has compactness and nonempty interior, so this does not arise.

glossary.plain: Compact convex set with nonempty interior, barycenter 0, and interior lattice points exactly {0}

glossary.note: The division is real division by n!, which is nonzero, so there is no junk.

lean_claims.plain: For every n, the barycenter of (n+1)Δ_n − (1,…,1) is 0.
For n>0 there is a compact convex full-dimensional body with barycenter 0 and int ∩ Z^n = {0} whose volume is (n+1)^n/n!.
For n>0 and S ⊂ R^n convex, compact, with nonempty interior, barycenter 0 and int(S) ∩ Z^n = {0}: vol(S) ≤ (n+1)^n/n!.

paper_claims.plain: A full-dimensional compact convex body K ⊂ R^n with barycenter 0 and int(K) ∩ Z^n = {0} satisfies vol(K) ≤ (n+1)^n/n!.
The simplex (n+1)Δ_n − (1,…,1) has barycenter 0, no other interior lattice point, and volume (n+1)^n/n!.

coverage.why: Same hypotheses (convex, compact, nonempty interior, barycenter 0, interior lattice points = {0}) and same bound. The n>0 restriction is the natural reading and n=0 is not discussed in the excerpt.
Existence of an extremizer; the barycenter and volume of the specific simplex are given by the other two theorems.
Barycenter of the centered simplex is 0.

flags.explanation: `barycenter` is 0 whenever the volume is 0 or the integrand is non-integrable. In the main theorem, compactness and nonempty interior give positive finite volume and integrability, so `barycenter S = 0` is the genuine condition. The same holds in `CenteredBody`.
flags.probe_idea: Prove: IsCompact K → (interior K).Nonempty → 0 < normalizedVolume K, and that the integral over K of the identity is integrable.

flags.explanation: The name suggests a normalization but the definition is plain Lebesgue volume, which is what the paper's vol(K) is. Cosmetic only.

lint_verdicts.why: Only matters for non-integrable or null-volume sets; the target statements assume compact convex with nonempty interior, so the integral is a genuine Bochner integral.
The denominator n! is a positive real, so there is no division by zero.
